raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Adds encoder (ViT) CUDA graph capture/replay support to
`PaddleOCRVLForConditionalGeneration`, implementing the
`SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` protocol introduced by the shared framework in
#42224.

Closes / contributes to #38175 (umbrella: encoder CUDA graph support for VLMs).

**Duplicate-work check** (per AGENTS.md — no open PR found):
```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "PaddleOCR cudagraph in:title,body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "paddleocr encoder"
```

### Background

vLLM's LLM decoder already benefits from CUDA graphs, but the vision encoder
runs eagerly — its many small kernel launches (patch embed, attention, MLP ×27
layers) dominate time-to-first-token (TTFT) for image requests. Capturing the
encoder into a CUDA graph removes per-launch CPU dispatch overhead.

This PR follows the same pattern as the Qwen2-VL (#41736), Kimi-VL (#41992),
and Step3-VL (#42224) implementations under #38175.

### What changed and why

PaddleOCR-VL's SigLIP vision tower had four patterns that prevented CUDA graph
capture. Each required moving data-dependent work into a precompute step outside
the graph:

| Location | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `SiglipVisionEmbeddings.forward` | Per-image `F.interpolate(size=(h,w))` — dynamic output shape per image | Precompute `position_embeddings` in `prepare_encoder_metadata`; graph path adds them with a fixed `+` op |
| `SiglipEncoder.forward` | Per-image Python loop + `pids.max()` host sync to build 2D RoPE | Precompute `rotary_pos_emb` and `max_seqlen` outside the graph; pass as optional args |
| `encode_image` | Builds `cu_seqlens` from Python lists, one image at a time | Replaced by a single batched path with precomputed, padded `cu_seqlens` |
| `Projector (mlp_AR)` | Per-image `rearrange("(t h p1 w p2) d → ...")` — reshape layout depends on `h,w` | Precompute a `merge_index` gather order; graph uses a static `index_select` + reshape (`Projector.forward_packed`) |

The projector runs **inside** the captured graph (covering the full SigLIP
encoder + spatial-merge projection). The existing per-image eager path is fully
preserved — all precomputed-buffer arguments are optional; `encoder_metadata=None`
runs the original logic unchanged with zero behaviour change when
`cudagraph_mm_encoder=False`.

The graph is automatically **disabled** for non-FA attention backends (e.g.
`TORCH_SDPA` on pre-SM80 GPUs) — `get_encoder_cudagraph_config` returns empty
`modalities` in that case and the manager falls back to eager transparently.
Image-only; no video support.

### Key new symbols

| Symbol | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `SiglipVisionModel.prepare_encoder_metadata` | `paddleocr_vl.py` | Eagerly builds all fixed-shape buffers: `position_embeddings`, `rotary_pos_emb`, `cu_seqlens` (padded), `max_seqlen`, `merge_index` |
| `Projector.forward_packed` | `paddleocr_vl.py` | Fixed-shape spatial merge via `merge_index` gather — the projector path captured in the graph |
| `_pad_paddleocr_cu_seqlens_buffer` | `paddleocr_vl.py` | Replay padding logic that keeps `cu_seqlens[-1]` (total patch count) invariant between capture and replay |
| `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` protocol methods (×10) | `paddleocr_vl.py` | Full protocol implementation on `PaddleOCRVLForConditionalGeneration` |

---

## Test Plan

```bash
# 1. Numerical parity — metadata-driven graph path == per-image eager path
#    Runs on any CUDA GPU (fp32, ~5 s), no model download needed.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_paddleocr_vl_cudagraph.py -v

# 2. MRoPE regression — existing eager path unchanged
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_paddleocr_vl_mrope.py -v

# 3. End-to-end capture/replay — dummy weights, no download, requires SM >= 8.0
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  "tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py::test_vit_cudagraph_image[paddleocr_vl]" \
  -v --timeout=300

# 4. TTFT latency benchmark (real model, A10G)
# Graph OFF — baseline
.venv/bin/vllm bench latency \
  --model PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --input-len 16 \
  --output-len 1 \
  --batch-size 8 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": {"count": 1, "width": 896, "height": 896}}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  -cc.cudagraph_mm_encoder=false

# Graph ON
.venv/bin/vllm bench latency \
  --model PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --input-len 16 \
  --output-len 1 \
  --batch-size 8 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": {"count": 1, "width": 896, "height": 896}}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  -cc.cudagraph_mm_encoder=true \
  -cc.encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets="[4096]"
```

---

## Test Results

**Hardware:** NVIDIA A10G (SM 8.6, 24 GB VRAM),
bfloat16, FlashAttention 2, batch=8, 896×896 images, `output-len=1`
(TTFT-focused: minimises decode time so encoder dominates measured latency).

Graph capture confirmed in logs:
```
Using AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN for MMEncoderAttention.
EncoderCudaGraphManager initialized with budgets=[1024, 4096], max_batch_size=128
Encoder CUDA graph capture complete. Captured 2 budget graphs.
```

### TTFT latency

| Metric | Graph OFF | Graph ON | Improvement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Avg latency | 11.93 ms | 11.23 ms | **↓ 5.9%** |
| P50 latency | 11.93 ms | 11.20 ms | **↓ 6.1%** |
| P99 latency | 12.46 ms | 11.66 ms | **↓ 6.5%** |
| Iterations/s | 83.65 | 88.92 | **↑ 6.3%** |

I don't think the TTFT numbers in the description measure the encoder at all. `vllm bench latency` only builds random-token `TokensPrompt`s (vllm/benchmarks/latency.py), so no image is ever sent; `--limit-mm-per-prompt` only affects memory profiling. The ~6% delta is therefore noise or a side effect of graph capture, not the ViT graph.

Could you re-measure with a workload that actually carries images, e.g. `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random-mm` with a fixed 896x896 bucket, and report TTFT plus encoder time with graph on/off?

I used this command to bench the encoder in my history PR:

```bash
vllm bench mm-processor \
--model /shared/models/modelscope/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR \
--max-model-len 8192 \
--dataset-name random-mm \
--random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 \
--random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0.0 \
--random-mm-bucket-config '{(896, 896, 1): 1.0}' \
--random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 0}' \
--num-prompts 100 \
--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true, "encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch": 8}'
```

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Encoder CUDA graph parity tests for a tiny random PaddleOCR-VL vision tower.
+
+The graph path precomputes the per-image metadata on the host and pads the
+inputs to a fixed batch shape, so its output must match the eager path.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from transformers.models.paddleocr_vl.configuration_paddleocr_vl import (
+    PaddleOCRVLConfig,
+)
+
+from vllm.config import MultiModalConfig, get_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.model_executor.models.paddleocr_vl import (
+    PaddleOCRVLForConditionalGeneration,
+    Projector,
+    SiglipVisionModel,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import AttentionBackendEnum
+from vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph import EncoderCudaGraphManager
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda_alike(),
+    reason="The vision rotary embedding and CUDA graphs need CUDA or ROCm.",
+)
+
+DEVICE = torch.device("cuda")
+DTYPE = torch.float32
+PATCH_SIZE = 14
+MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 4
+
+# Multi-image batches as (t, h, w) patch grids; h and w are multiples of the
+# 2x2 spatial merge size.
+BATCH_SMALL = [(1, 2, 2), (1, 4, 2)]
+BATCH_MIXED = [(1, 4, 6), (1, 8, 4), (1, 2, 2)]
+BATCH_FULL = [(1, 10, 8), (1, 4, 4), (1, 2, 6), (1, 2, 2)]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def make_model(dist_init):
+    """Build a tiny PaddleOCR-VL vision tower and projector with random weights.
+
+    Only the modules used by the encoder are built; the language model is not.
+    """
+
+    def _make(
+        attn_backend: AttentionBackendEnum | None = None,
+    ) -> PaddleOCRVLForConditionalGeneration:
+        config = PaddleOCRVLConfig(
+            vision_config=dict(
+                hidden_size=64,
+                intermediate_size=128,
+                num_attention_heads=4,
+                num_hidden_layers=2,
+                image_size=56,
+                patch_size=PATCH_SIZE,
+            ),
+            text_config=dict(hidden_size=32),
+        )
+        vllm_config = get_current_vllm_config()
+        old_model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+        if attn_backend is not None:
+            vllm_config.model_config = SimpleNamespace(
+                multimodal_config=MultiModalConfig(mm_encoder_attn_backend=attn_backend)
+            )
+        old_dtype = torch.get_default_dtype()
+        torch.set_default_dtype(DTYPE)
+        try:
+            with torch.device(DEVICE):
+                model = object.__new__(PaddleOCRVLForConditionalGeneration)
+                torch.nn.Module.__init__(model)
+                model.config = config
+                model.visual = SiglipVisionModel(config.vision_config)
+                model.mlp_AR = Projector(config.text_config, config.vision_config)
+        finally:
+            torch.set_default_dtype(old_dtype)
+            vllm_config.model_config = old_model_config
+
+        if attn_backend is not None:
+            assert model.visual.vision_model.encoder.attn_backend == attn_backend
+
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        for param in model.parameters():
+            torch.nn.init.normal_(param, std=0.05)
+        return model.eval()
+
+    return _make
+
+
+def make_mm_kwargs(grids: list[tuple[int, int, int]]) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    num_patches = sum(t * h * w for t, h, w in grids)
+    return {
+        "pixel_values": torch.randn(
+            num_patches, 3, PATCH_SIZE, PATCH_SIZE, device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE
+        ),
+        "image_grid_thw": torch.tensor(grids, dtype=torch.long),
+    }
+
+
+def copy_replay_into_capture_buffers(
+    buffers: dict[str, torch.Tensor], replay: dict[str, torch.Tensor | None]
+) -> None:
+    """Copy replay values into capture buffers as EncoderCudaGraphManager does."""
+    for key, buf in buffers.items():
+        src = replay.get(key)
+        if src is None:
+            continue
+        if src.ndim == 0:
+            buf.copy_(src)
+        else:
+            EncoderCudaGraphManager._copy_padded_buffer(buf, src)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("grids", [BATCH_SMALL, BATCH_MIXED, BATCH_FULL])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_cudagraph_forward_matches_eager(make_model, grids):
+    """The graph forward on precomputed replay buffers must match eager."""
+    model = make_model()
+    torch.manual_seed(1)
+    mm_kwargs = make_mm_kwargs(grids)
+
+    eager = model.encoder_eager_forward(mm_kwargs)
+    replay = model.prepare_encoder_cudagraph_replay_buffers(
+        mm_kwargs, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE
+    ).values
+    graph = model.encoder_cudagraph_forward(dict(replay))
+
+    num_tokens = sum(t * (h // 2) * (w // 2) for t, h, w in grids)
+    assert eager.shape == (num_tokens, model.config.text_config.hidden_size)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(graph, eager, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4)
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_padded_capture_replay_matches_eager(make_model):
+    """One captured graph, padded to a larger budget, replays different batches.
+
+    A real ``torch.cuda.graph`` capture fails on host syncs, and replaying two
+    batches of different sizes checks that the zero padding leaves the real
+    rows unchanged.
+    """
+    model = make_model(AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN)
+    token_budget = 64
+    capture = model.prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs(
+        token_budget, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, DEVICE, DTYPE
+    ).values
+    buffers = dict(capture)
+
+    # Warm up (Triton autotuning/compilation) before capturing.
+    model.encoder_cudagraph_forward(dict(buffers))
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        output = model.encoder_cudagraph_forward(dict(buffers))
+    assert output.shape[0] == token_budget
+
+    torch.manual_seed(1)
+    for grids in (BATCH_MIXED, BATCH_FULL):
+        mm_kwargs = make_mm_kwargs(grids)
+        eager = model.encoder_eager_forward(mm_kwargs)
+        replay = model.prepare_encoder_cudagraph_replay_buffers(
+            mm_kwargs, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE
+        ).values
+        copy_replay_into_capture_buffers(buffers, replay)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            output[: eager.shape[0]], eager, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4
+        )

reviews.body: Sorry for late reply, I'm busy with working these days. Btw, could you please rebase on the latest main and resolve the conflicts?

I don't think the TTFT numbers in the description measure the encoder at all. `vllm bench latency` only builds random-token `TokensPrompt`s (vllm/benchmarks/latency.py), so no image is ever sent; `--limit-mm-per-prompt` only affects memory profiling. The ~6% delta is therefore noise or a side effect of graph capture, not the ViT graph.

Could you re-measure with a workload that actually carries images, e.g. `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random-mm` with a fixed 896x896 bucket, and report TTFT plus encoder time with graph on/off?

I used this command to bench the encoder in my history PR:

```bash
vllm bench mm-processor \
--model /shared/models/modelscope/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR \
--max-model-len 8192 \
--dataset-name random-mm \
--random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 \
--random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0.0 \
--random-mm-bucket-config '{(896, 896, 1): 1.0}' \
--random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 0}' \
--num-prompts 100 \
--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true, "encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch": 8}'
```
